messages.subject: [statnet_help] Importing Pajek file with partition?
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I've been going through for various Statnet tutorials and papers for the 
last couple weeks now, and am finally getting down to running some of my

messages.subject: [statnet_help] TNT MCMC Sampler
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I'm looking into the details of Statnet's implementation of the MCMC algorithm for simulating draws from ERGM.

Morris et al ("Specification of Exponential-Family Random Graph Models: Terms and Computational Aspects." 2008, in J. Stat. Soft. v24) says that Statnet by default implements a "tie-no-tie sampler". The paper says the sampler "chooses an empty dyad with probability 1/2".

However, I have been looking at the C source code for the sampler (MH_TNT() in MHproposals.c - version from CRAN today), and my reading of this implies a slightly different algorithm has been implemented. It appears to me a tie (rather than empty dyad) is selected at random with probability 1/2, and otherwise any dyad is selected. This doesn't seem to me to be the same as the sampler described in Morris et al. It is very possible I am not fully understanding the C though - I wonder if there is documentation somewhere that confirms whether this has changed?

I'd be grateful for any help.

Many thanks,

Robert Goudie

-- 
Ph.D. Student
Department of Statistics
University of Warwick

messages.subject: [statnet_help] TNT MCMC Sampler
messages.body_plain:
Hi Robert.  Coincidentally, I was just looking at that same patch of  
code with a grad student.  You are correct:  The TNT proposal does not  
choose an empty dyad with probability 1/2; in fact, this probability  
is actually somewhat less than 50% in the current implementation.  It  
would certainly be possible to modify this code (by allowing the  
function to change the value of the "comp" variable) so that the  
probability is exactly 50%, but when comp=0.5 as it is presently set,  
your description below is correct.

For a sparse graph, the probability of choosing an empty dyad is close  
to 50%, but nevertheless the description in the article is not accurate.

Sorry we did not catch that error in the article!

Dave

messages.subject: [statnet_help] TNT MCMC Sampler
messages.body_plain:
Hi David. Many thanks for your emails clearing up my question about the sampler.

For the sampler implemented, I think there may be a problem with a minor edge case. (Again, it is very possible I am not fully understanding the C.) The case involves proposals to and from the empty graph - so clearly in practice this isn't an important issue.

Suppose current graph y. Draw proposal y' from proposal density Q. Suppose y has 1 edge, and y' is the empty graph. Then,

Q(y |y') = 1/ndyads [rather than (1-comp)/ndyads, since can't remove an edge from an empty graph]
Q(y'|y ) = comp/nedges + (1 - comp)/ndyads = comp + (1 - comp)/ndyads

Hastings factor 
= 1/(comp * ndyads + (1 - comp))
!= nedges/(odds * ndyads + nedges)
= 1/(odds * ndyads + 1)

The case when y is the empty graph, y' is a graph with 1 edge is similar.

Thanks again,

Robert Goudie

-- 
Ph.D. Student
Department of Statistics
University of Warwick

messages.body_plain:
Hi Robert.   Nice catch -- you're correct about the case of moving  
from the empty graph to the one-edge graph and vice-versa.  We will  
fix this in the next release of ergm.

Incidentally, this bug is as you point out almost never an issue in  
practice, but it is possible to construct an example specifically to  
reveal it:
x <- network(1-diag(3),dir=F)
s <- simulate(x~edges, nsim=1e+4, theta0=-2, interval=100, statsonly=T)

In this example of an undirected 3-node network, the expected number  
of edges is 3*exp(-2)/(1+exp(-2)), which is
 > 3*exp(-2)/(1+exp(-2))
[1] 0.3576088

Yet what I get from the simulation is consistently too high.
 > mean(s)
[1] 0.5404

I suspect this may be due to the bias introduced by the Hastings ratio  
problem.

Dave
